body.p: , completing . Headers: xml.h (needs tree.h) < processor.h (xdm.h, xml.h) < xpath.h; serialize.h needs only xdm.h (it serializes from an item heap).

item.p: XML parser: a reusable object (allocator, name pool, sxml_xml_limits: depth, entity expansion bytes) that parses a whole document in memory into any sxml_tree_builder, or only checks it (sxml check). Failures are interface statuses (MALFORMED_INPUT, INVALID_UTF8, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for other encodings, LIMIT_EXCEEDED) with a diagnostic naming the failed production or WFC: well-formedness errors have no QName codes; fn:doc and fn:parse-xml turn them into FODC0002 and FODC0006. Nothing outside the input is read.

Processor: pool, registry and heap in its memory, one allocator for everything, one limits struct, a resource resolver and a clock; sxml_processor_parse_document gives an owned document node whose arena tree destroys itself when unreferenced.

Resource resolver: one resolve operation with an sxml_resource_kind (only XML_DOCUMENT now; text, XQuery modules and XSLT stylesheet modules later), after Saxon's ResourceResolver, so later phases add kinds instead of publishing new interfaces. It answers bytes (sxml parses them with the processor's limits), a document node, or none. "Not available" (a missing file, a refused URI, a failed read) is SXML_RESOURCE_FORM_NONE, which fn:doc raises as FODC0002; a failure status ( included) stops the evaluation. The null resolver makes nothing available (the library does no I/O); the default implementation and test double is sxml_table_resource_resolver over in-memory entries.
Clock: read at most once per evaluation, so fn:current-dateTime is stable; sxml_system_clock (C17 timespec_get, implicit timezone UTC) and sxml_fixed_clock.

Contexts: sxml_static_context_configuration and sxml_dynamic_context_configuration are plain structs embedded by value in requests; zero means the default context. XQuery and XSLT reuse them. Names are name pool identifiers and types registry identifiers, as in the substrate. External variables are declared with a type and bound by name (coerced, XPTY0004; unbound XPDY0002); the context value is a sequence (XPath 4.0) with a presence flag; available documents make fn:doc(uri) the very node bound elsewhere (QT4 sources with a uri). A namespace binding with prefix 0 is the default namespace for elements and types.

Expressions: sxml_xpath_expression follows the lifecycle quintet; initialize compiles. The compiled form is allocated from the processor and counted, so inline function items in a result outlive the expression (). Results are complete: nothing lazy that can fail later. Evaluations may nest. sxml_xpath_parse_sequence_type turns declared types given as text (279 QT4 param ... as=) into sequence types.

Serialization: sxml_output_stream (one write, which returns 's status when the platform refuses), the sxml_output_buffer as default and test double, and sxml_serialize_sequence with the adaptive method; the method enum and parameters struct grow in Phase 3.
Limits: 0 means no bound, except maximum_expression_depth and maximum_evaluation_depth, where 0 means sxml's default: no bound would mean a C stack overflow.

Left out until needed, each a new field that designated initializers keep source-compatible: host extension functions in the static context (meanwhile a function item bound to a variable), decimal formats, collations, default language, fn:trace output, cancellation, a seed for fn:random-number-generator.
